blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At this level, communicating with IT support is less about asking nicely and more about making the first message complete. Every back-and-forth is time everyone loses. A five-sentence message that contains what you were doing, what happened, the error code if any, what you tried, and how reproducible the problem is often saves thirty minutes of conversation.

Good requesters also match the urgency to reality. A blocked process that stops the whole team deserves a direct call and a clear statement: 'this is blocking twelve people'. A minor annoyance can wait for the normal queue. Mixing the two — flagging small things as urgent — quickly erodes the help desk's trust, and genuinely urgent things then arrive alongside less important ones.

The help desk said that the best requesters always wrote clear first messages and matched urgency honestly. That is the rise-level skill in one sentence.

items.q: According to the text, what makes communication with IT support effective at this level?
items.why: "communicating with IT support is less about asking nicely and more about making the first message complete".

items.q: What five things should a complete first message contain?
options: What you were doing, what happened, the error code, what you tried, and how reproducible it is
The requester's name, team, role, manager and location
A greeting, an apology, a request, a deadline and a thank-you
The date, time, device, browser and network
items.why: O parágrafo lista exatamente esses cinco elementos da mensagem de cinco frases.

items.q: Why should you reserve 'urgent' for problems that block the whole team?
options: Because false urgency erodes the help desk's trust
Because urgent tickets are always cheaper to fix
Because minor problems cannot be logged in the queue
Because the help desk only reads urgent messages
items.why: "flagging small things as urgent — quickly erodes the help desk's trust".

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Calling something urgent when it is not is a smart way to get faster help
Trust with the help desk is worth protecting
A clear first message can save both sides a lot of time
Urgency should reflect real business impact
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que a falsa urgência destrói a confiança — portanto não é uma boa estratégia.

items.q: The phrase 'this is blocking twelve people' suggests that…
options: the help desk counts how many tickets you send
urgency is more convincing when tied to concrete impact
twelve is the minimum number for an urgent request
only large teams should contact IT support
items.why: Inferência: dar um número concreto mostra o impacto real e justifica a urgência de forma honesta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver orientando uma nova gerente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before you send your first ticket to IT, let me walk you through how I'd frame it. I told the last person I coached the same thing: your goal is to end the conversation in one message, not to start ten of them.

Picture what happened this morning. The reporting tool froze while you were exporting the month-end file. Don't just write 'it's broken, please help'. Tell them what you were doing, what actually happened, the error code on the screen, what you already tried — say, closing and reopening — and whether it happens every single time or just once. That last part matters more than people think.

Now, on urgency. When the finance team can't close the books, that's a real emergency, so you call and you say plainly, 'this is blocking the whole close'. But when your mouse feels a little slow, that goes in the normal queue. The moment you start marking everything urgent, they stop believing you — and then your genuine emergencies wait behind everyone else's noise. Match the flag to reality, every time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver say the goal of a support message should be?
options: To send at least ten messages
To start a long conversation with the help desk
To end the conversation in one message
To avoid writing and always call
items.why: "your goal is to end the conversation in one message, not to start ten of them."

items.q: According to Oliver, which detail do people underestimate?
options: Whether the problem happens every time or just once
The name of the reporting tool
The colour of the error message
The exact time the problem happened
items.why: "whether it happens every single time or just once. That last part matters more than people think."

items.q: How should the manager handle a slightly slow mouse?
options: Put it in the normal queue
Wait until it stops working completely
Mark it as urgent to be safe
items.why: "when your mouse feels a little slow, that goes in the normal queue."

items.q: What does Oliver imply happens if you mark everything urgent?
options: IT gives you a dedicated contact
Your real emergencies get delayed behind everyone else
The help desk answers you faster
items.why: Inferência: "they stop believing you — and then your genuine emergencies wait behind everyone else's noise."

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's approach to coaching here?
options: Practical, using a concrete example to make his point
Focused only on being polite to IT
items.why: Inferência: ele usa o caso concreto da ferramenta de relatórios para ensinar de forma prática e direta.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "If the problem is not reproducible, the technician struggles to diagnose it." Reproducible means…
options: able to be made to happen again
items.why: Reproducible = reproduzível: que pode ser feito acontecer de novo, o que ajuda o diagnóstico.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please include the ___ shown on the screen so IT can look it up."
items.why: Error code = código de erro: o identificador que a IT consulta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Non-urgent tickets simply wait in the normal ___ until a technician is free."
items.why: Queue = fila: onde os chamados esperam atendimento.

items.q: "Every extra back-and-forth delays the fix." Back-and-forth refers to…
options: the repeated exchange of messages between two sides
items.why: Back-and-forth = ida e volta: a troca repetida de mensagens entre você e a IT.

items.q: "Constantly crying wolf will erode the help desk's trust." To erode means to…
items.why: To erode = erodir: desgastar aos poucos — aqui, a confiança.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns ao lidar com suporte de TI. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "A senior technician has to sign off on the fix before it goes live." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "IT will roll out the patch to all offices next week." To roll out means to…
options: implement across the organisation in stages
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva, aqui em todos os escritórios.

items.q: "If you don't hear back, follow up on the ticket the next day." To follow up means to…
options: check on progress and remind them
items.why: Follow up = dar seguimento: verificar o andamento e lembrar do pedido.

items.q: "When the system crashed, IT had to look into the root cause." To look into means to…
items.why: Look into = investigar, examinar a fundo.

items.q: "Marking every ticket urgent won't move the needle on response time." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, nenhuma.
